studies.organism: Macaca fascicularis, M. mulatta and M. nemestrina; C57/BL6 mouse
studies.preparation: Isolated whole-mount OFF RGC recordings, with species-specific adaptation and light calibration; additional cell and slice experiments in the paper are not merged into these contexts.
studies.observable: Excitatory synaptic input to OFF parasol (primate) and OFF sustained alpha (mouse) RGCs before and during LY/APB.
studies.finding: The paired pharmacological responses differ with species and background; the experiment identifies primary versus combined non-primary routing more strongly than it identifies secondary versus tertiary contributions.
limitations: Isolated retina without normal pigment regeneration; prolonged adaptation and in vivo neuromodulation were not tested.
LY/APB affects all ON bipolar pathways and may have additional effects; residual signaling does not uniquely distinguish secondary from tertiary routes.
OFF parasol responses at the high background can include substantial cone drive. Species are pooled within the reported macaque cohort; individual animals are not resolved by the summary spreadsheet.
Figure 6F spreadsheet contains summary amplitudes, not individual samples or SEM.

The modulation frequency of the six Figure 6F summary rows is not resolved by the reviewed metadata. Do not import 2 Hz from the separate A-C or supplement experiment; no fully specified replication protocol is claimed.

studies.preparation: Dark-adapted isolated whole mounts, 2-6 month mice of either sex, separate rod- and cone-specific Cx36 KO lines and corresponding wild-type littermate controls.
studies.observable: Loose-patch, baseline-subtracted peak firing response of transient OFF alpha RGCs at light offset.
studies.finding: Genetic and pharmacological contrasts support a secondary rod-pathway contribution in the selected dark-adapted flash protocol, without making a universal statement about other cell classes or light adaptation.
limitations: Constitutive cell-specific Cx36 deletion is not an acute isolated edge removal; the two mutant lines are separate comparisons.
APB blocks ON pathways and changes crossover inhibition and basal firing; its effect is not a calibrated contribution weight.
Fully dark-adapted flash measurements in B6-background transient OFF alpha cells do not transfer to sustained OFF alpha cells or adapting sinusoidal backgrounds.
Supplementary files and original electrophysiology traces were not independently reanalysed.
